audit_findings.title: The bridge may omit a large portfolio of long-term government securities
audit_findings.mechanism: The omitted non-operating securities enter the equity bridge after portfolio interest income is removed from owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $138.4 million, short-term investments of $464.0 million, and long-term U.S. Government bond investments of $353.0 million for a total of $955.4 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error, not merely a possibility. June 30, 2026 cash of $120.563 million plus short-term investments of $350.749 million exactly equals the $471.312 million bridge, while the same filing separately reports $383.229 million of long-term U.S. Government bonds. Adding them would increase base value from $52.02 to about $60.28 per share, a 15.9% increase in base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Add the $383.229 million June 30 long-term government-bond fair value to the bridge and rerun every scenario and buy-below price, after confirming no associated interest income remains in owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may capitalize economics from an expired major-customer agreement
audit_findings.magnitude: renewed at least through 2030, five years beyond the former end-2025 term (filed); economic changes unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The agreement affects the durability of customer revenue embedded in anchor owner earnings and near-term growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2021, we and LG Display entered into new agreements that extended the terms of these agreements at least through the end of 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied June 2026 filing resolves the alleged expiration: LG Display entered into new agreements in 2026 extending the license and supply arrangements at least through 2030. There is therefore no demonstrated post-2025 contract gap to correct. Undisclosed pricing or other changed economics remain a business-performance question, but they do not support the specific claim that the valuation perpetuates an expired agreement.
audit_findings.action: Do not rerun for expiration. Obtain any disclosed renewal economics and compare 2026 LG-related revenue, margins and cash receipts with FY2025; rerun only if that evidence demonstrates weaker recurring economics.

audit_findings.title: Positive terminal growth may be incompatible with erosion of the foundational patent moat
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $784.2 million to $1,179.9 million of terminal-value operating PV is exposed (computed from the scenario operating PV and 47.7%-51.5% terminal shares)
audit_findings.mechanism: A weaker post-patent moat would reduce long-run owner earnings and may require declining or finite-life cash flows instead of 2.5% perpetual terminal growth.
audit_findings.evidence: While we hold a wide range of additional patents and patent applications relating to our commercial OLED materials and technologies whose expiration dates extend (and in the case of patent applications, will extend) beyond 2025, many of which are also of importance in the OLED industry, none may be of an equally essential nature as our original fundamental patents, and therefore our competitive position may be less certain as a result of the expiration of these patents.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated loss of economics. The filing acknowledges that successor patents may not be as essential as the expired foundational patents, while the valuation assigns roughly half of operating value to a growing perpetuity. Because even the bear case eventually uses 2.5% terminal growth, none of the supplied scenarios tests structural decline; the exposed value is large enough to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build declining and finite-life terminal cases using evidence from post-expiration licensing rates, material pricing, customer retention, patent-family coverage and 2026 commercial performance; compare them with the current scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded retirement promise may be an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $57.166 million reported noncurrent liability at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.23 per valuation share and 2.4% of base equity value; $77.2 million of disclosed remaining payments equals 3.2% of base equity value before discounting (filed/computed)
audit_findings.mechanism: Any opening unfunded obligation not already captured by projected pension expense and cash payments would be deducted in the equity bridge or explicitly forecast through owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Payments towards the retirement plan obligations commenced during fiscal year 2023 and are expected to total $77.2 million over the remaining life of the plan.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation is demonstrated, but omission from value is not: owner earnings may already retain service and interest costs, and the record does not show how those items were projected. Even treating the full $57.166 million liability as an additional deduction reduces base value by only about $1.23 per share; even the undiscounted $77.2 million payment total is only 3.2% of the $2.413 billion base equity value and cannot close the $30.32 gap between base value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile projected SERP expense and benefit payments to owner earnings. Deduct the June 2026 funded-status deficit only to the extent the opening obligation is not already represented, and document the anti-double-counting treatment.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may perpetuate a revenue-estimate catch-up
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.1 million revenue increase less the separate $7.1 million reduction, for a net $7.0 million pre-tax FY2025 revenue increase (filed); owner-earnings and valuation effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in the anchor as recurring operating economics, the net positive adjustment increases owner earnings and all projected and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The cumulative catch-up adjustment recorded to revenue arising from changes in estimates of transaction price, net was an increase $14.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to an increase of $10.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting adjustments are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the owner-earnings calculation normalized them or how their tax and working-capital effects entered the $138.2 million anchor. The net reported revenue effect was positive and arose alongside lower expected customer demand, so inclusion could overstate recurring earning power. Continued catch-ups, including $10.0 million in the first half of 2026, also prevent treating the entire amount as plainly nonrecurring without a contract-level reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Trace both FY2025 adjustments through revenue, tax, receivables, deferred revenue and the owner-earnings worksheet. Rerun the valuation with only the after-tax cash-timing portion removed once that reconciliation establishes what remains in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling may not capture maximum PSU settlement
audit_findings.magnitude: a conservative gross 678,854 incremental shares above one-for-one settlement, or 1.46% of the 46.386266 million valuation denominator (computed from 237,121 year-end 2025 PSUs plus 102,306 first-half 2026 grants at the additional two-times payout); base value impact about $0.75 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Maximum PSU vesting increases the fully diluted share denominator and reduces per-share scenario values and buy-below prices without changing enterprise or equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum number of performance units that may vest based on performance is three times the shares granted.
audit_findings.explanation: The inability to split the latest combined award balance leaves a real denominator uncertainty, but its scale is not sufficient to change the conclusion. Even the conservative calculation that ignores intervening vesting and forfeitures and adds the full incremental maximum would increase shares to about 47.065 million, reducing base value from $52.02 to approximately $51.27 and buy-below from $36.41 to about $35.88.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 RSU and PSU inventory by grant, apply each PSU's maximum multiplier, subtract vested and forfeited units, reconcile against shares already included in the 46.386266 million ceiling, and update the denominator.
